back2basics.text: Panchayat and municipal elections are local body elections that enable democratic decentralisation by empowering elected representatives at the village and urban levels. These elections are conducted under the supervision of the Election Commission or local authorities to ensure free and fair voting. They are crucial for grassroots governance, development planning, and delivery of public services.

2026-11-21-pm-0c9d895a54.deck: Ladakh, India's high-altitude Union Territory, is conducting its first panchayat and municipal elections since 2019 on November 21, 2026. This election is notable for having the highest polling station at 15,057 feet, highlighting challenges in electoral administration in difficult terrain.

body.label: First elections since 2019
body.text: These are the first panchayat and municipal elections in Ladakh since it was carved out as a separate Union Territory from Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.

body.label: Polling stations at extreme altitudes
body.text: Polling stations are located from Drass at 10,800 feet to Korzok at 15,075 feet, making it the highest polling station in India.

body.label: Voter and area coverage
body.text: About 1.87 lakh electors are spread over 59,146 square kilometres, with elections held for 192 panchayat halqas and 1428 panchs.

body.label: Unopposed candidates
body.text: So far, 55 sarpanches and 1186 panch candidates have been elected unopposed, and in Kargil Municipal Council, four out of 17 wards have unopposed representatives.

body.label: Security and logistical arrangements
body.text: Election and security personnel were deployed with buses arranged to reach remote polling stations, ensuring free, fair, and peaceful elections.

back2basics.concept: HPV Vaccination and Cervical Cancer Prevention
back2basics.text: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is a virus that can cause cervical cancer in women. Vaccination against HPV is a preventive measure that protects individuals before they are exposed to the virus. Vaccines are typically given to adolescent girls to build immunity early. National immunisation campaigns use government health facilities and frontline workers to deliver vaccines safely and monitor adverse events. Digital platforms can support tracking and transparency in vaccination programs.

2026-11-21-pm-333e042f7b.deck: India has achieved a milestone by administering more than 1 crore doses of the HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls under a national campaign launched in February 2026. This progress is significant for cervical cancer prevention and reflects strong government coordination and public confidence in preventive healthcare.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about India's National HPV Vaccination Campaign:
1. The campaign provides free, voluntary single-dose HPV vaccination to 14-year-old girls with parental consent.

mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the six states with 100% coverage are Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar; Karnataka and Tamil Nadu have lower coverage percentages.

body.label: Campaign launch and target
body.text: Launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February 2026, the campaign provides free, safe, voluntary single-dose HPV vaccination to 14-year-old girls at government health facilities with parental consent.

body.label: Coverage achieved
body.text: The campaign has reached nearly 87% of the annual target cohort of approximately 1.2 crore girls, administering over 1 crore doses in less than nine months.

body.label: State-wise performance
body.text: Six states—Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar—have achieved 100% coverage of their target populations, with Uttar Pradesh vaccinating over 29.33 lakh girls.

sections.heading: What is the National HPV Vaccination Campaign and its coverage?

body.label: Centre-State coordination
body.text: Strong coordination between the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and state governments supports tailored approaches to reach rural, urban, and remote areas.

body.label: Community engagement
body.text: Healthcare professionals, school teachers, ASHAs, ANMs, and frontline workers actively engage parents and communities to build awareness and counter misinformation.

body.label: Digital monitoring
body.text: The U-WIN digital platform enables real-time monitoring, beneficiary tracking, vaccination slot booking, and issuance of digital certificates, enhancing transparency and accessibility.

body.label: Safety measures
body.text: Vaccination sessions are supervised by trained medical officers with 24×7 healthcare arrangements to manage rare adverse events following immunization (AEFI).

sections.heading: How is the campaign implemented and monitored?

body.label: Cause of cervical cancer
body.text: Persistent infection with high-risk types of Human Papillomavirus is responsible for the majority of cervical cancer cases.

body.label: Effectiveness of vaccination
body.text: HPV vaccination is a proven preventive intervention that reduces the risk of HPV infections leading to cervical cancer.

body.label: Timing of vaccination
body.text: Vaccinating girls at 14 years offers protection before potential exposure to HPV, contributing to long-term cervical cancer prevention.

sections.heading: Why does HPV vaccination matter for cervical cancer prevention?

Disaster management involves forecasting such events, issuing warnings, and implementing safety measures like evacuations and school closures to minimize damage and protect lives.

back2basics.concept: Indus Water Treaty and SCO framework
back2basics.text: The Indus Water Treaty is a water-sharing agreement between India and Pakistan, governing the use of rivers originating in India and flowing into Pakistan. The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) is a multilateral regional grouping that includes India and Pakistan as permanent members, providing a platform for dialogue and cooperation among member states.

2026-11-21-pm-a7538492db.deck: India reaffirmed its unchanged position on the Indus Water Treaty (IWT) during the visit of Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi in November 2026. This event marked a rare diplomatic engagement between the two countries following recent tensions, highlighting the complexity of bilateral water disputes within multilateral platforms.
